title: How should we split the groups?
hook: Four people, two baseline levels: compare two ways to assign them.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values

claims.text: Four people have baseline outcomes 0,0,10,10, and treatment adds 2. If each arm gets one low and one high person, what treated-minus-control mean results?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-blocked-randomization/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Four units have baselines[0,0,10,10], treatment adds2. Split low/low vs high/high gives observed difference12; block one low+one high in each arm gives2 exactly. Randomization here concerns allocation, not guaranteed balance in all samples.

claims.text: The blocked allocation retains difference 2; the unbalanced allocation retains 12. The same treatment rule operates in both, but the second comparison also contains a baseline gap.

claims.text: Blocking on this known prognostic feature forces both arms to contain the same baseline mix. It removes this source of allocation variation in the toy population; randomization alone does not guarantee exact balance in each realized draw.

claims.text: Baseline levels are 1 and 9. Each arm receives one of each; treatment adds 3. What difference follows? The shared baseline average cancels, leaving the stipulated treatment effect 3.
